l.i: Ah, unda grandi pauci pecunia: Ah, ære[?] non pauco fuerunt Vilia ligna paranda nobis.

main_text.l: 5 Immane collo ferre iugum ferus Victor coegit, nosque laboribus Duris fatigauit: nec agros Ulla quies releuauit artus.
6 Gentes coegit tristis ad exteras Fames precantem tendere dexteram: Ut pane ieiunos fiueret Assyrius, Phariúsve[?] ventres.
7 Ætas auorum perfida Numinis Neglexit almi legibus obsequi: Delicta quorum nunc nepotes Multa luunt vitiosiores.
8 Seruire fœdis turba spadonibus Victos adegit Barbara: nec iugum Tam turpe quis ceruice vindex, Tristéve seruitium remouit.
9 Inuecta magno farra periculo Nostris fuerunt urbibus, & cibi Stricto virentes quum per agros Ense ferox equitaret hostis.
10 Nobis camino nigrior est cutis, Genisque pallor tristibus incubat, Orisque splendorem venusti Esuries truculenta perdit.

page.notes: The first stanza has no verse number and is set without a number in the printed text. The word "ære" in line 2 is partly unclear, possibly with a superscript mark. "Phariúsve" and "sæuiunt" are doubtful in the scan. The final line of the page is cut off at the lower edge and is partly illegible. No marginal notes or catchword are printed. The line "Victor" in stanza 5 keeps the printed ct ligature as read.
